title: Nonzero homology class produces a rank-one derived map
statement: Let S be any ring, K a derived object of ModuleCat S (in the stated lifted universe), and n an integer. If x in Hⁿ(K) is nonzero, there exists a nonzero morphism from the degree-zero single complex on ULift S to K⟦n⟧. Assume the derived category and the stated coproducts exist.

source.place: projective-source localization comparison, specialized to the rank-one single complex

proof.text: Take L = Q.objPreimage(K[n]) and its canonical isomorphism Q(L) ≅ K[n]. The shift-sequence isomorphism H⁰(K[n]) ≅ Hⁿ(K), functorial transport across this isomorphism, and homologyFunctorFactors identify Hⁿ(K) with H⁰(L). Apply this isomorphism to x to obtain a nonzero class y. All comparisons here are Mathlib isomorphisms.

The epimorphism L.homologyπ 0 is surjective by ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective. Choose a cycle z mapping to y. The linear map g : ULift S → L.cycles 0 given by a ↦ a.down • z exists as ULift.moduleEquiv.toLinearMap.smulRight z. Compose with L.iCycles 0 and apply HomologicalComplex.mkHomFromSingle; the required chain condition follows from iCycles_d. Localize this chain map f and postcompose with Q(L) ≅ K[n].

If the resulting derived morphism is zero, cancel the representative isomorphism to get Q.map f = 0. Naturality of DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors and cancellation of its invertible component then imply HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f 0 = 0.

Use HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap_i and mkHomFromSingle_f to identify cyclesMap f 0 with singleObjCyclesSelfIso.hom followed by g, cancelling the monomorphism L.iCycles 0. HomologicalComplex.homologyπ_naturality and the zero homology map show g ≫ L.homologyπ 0 = 0, after cancelling singleObjCyclesSelfIso.hom. Evaluate at ULift.up 1: the left side is y, hence y = 0, a contradiction.

proof_origin.place: rank-one specialization; explicit cycle construction using Mathlib homology naturality, without needing projective-source localization bijectivity
